items.title: Give new players time to make their first move
items.what: The first bout shows HasanAbi scoring an IPPON at 29 seconds and a 2½–0 win at 27 seconds. The result screen arrives roughly three seconds after the 30-second start.
items.why: A touch player can lose before they have worked out either stick, making the first match feel unwinnable.
items.how: Make the opening bout a short guided exchange: pause the clock until the player performs a stance move and a technique, then allow the opponent to score.

items.title: Show one executable move before the FIGHT button
items.what: The qualifier intro shows the opponent’s description and a large FIGHT button, but no control instruction. The small STANCE and TECHNIQUE direction key appears only on the live fight screen, above the sticks.
items.why: Players must learn two unfamiliar controls while the 30-second clock is already running.
items.how: Add a two-step prompt to the intro: move the left stick to step, then push the right stick forward for Lunge Punch. Let the player try both before enabling FIGHT.

items.title: Make stick directions readable under thumbs
items.what: On the portrait fight screen, the small gray arrows around both bottom joysticks nearly disappear against their dark brown rings, especially the left and right arrows.
items.why: The arrows are the only persistent directional cues once the instruction key is gone, and fingers will cover part of each stick.
items.how: Increase arrow size and contrast on the controls—not the dojo—and highlight the selected direction with the existing gold or blue accent.

items.title: Separate the point callout from the move name
items.what: In the IPPON screenshot, the SPINNING BACK KICK pill crosses the lower part of the large IPPON lettering, while HASANABI sits immediately beneath it.
items.why: The most important scoring moment becomes harder to read at a glance.
items.how: Give the scoring callout its own reserved area; move the technique pill below the callout or delay it until the IPPON animation has cleared.

items.title: Make loading progress visibly progress
items.what: On the pre-boot screen, “Downloading the game” sits above a very thin, low-contrast bar that appears unfilled in the screenshot.
items.why: On a phone, players cannot tell whether the download is advancing or stalled.
items.how: Keep the dark branded screen, but thicken the track, give its fill a distinct warm-gold color, and show a percentage or downloaded amount beside the status.
